text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

You are a man, the appointee is a man, and the panel were men. An all-male panel can disadvantage women candidates — it cannot plausibly explain a man being passed over for another man. Raising it would weaken your credibility on the points that actually help you.

Your real argument is the qualifications comparison: a master's in educational leadership and five years as deputy principal against "courses in school leadership" and classroom experience only. On paper you are the better-qualified candidate for a leadership post, and the panel owes you reasons.

Send a written follow-up citing your earlier request, set a deadline, and ask specifically which criteria were used and how each candidate scored.
